copy.hero_headline: New York already commutes by water. We make it a network.
copy.hero_sub: A connected employer water network across the harbor, Gold Coast, Long Island, and Connecticut — electric hydrofoil vessels, terminal-to-terminal, above the traffic and the toll.

copy.precedent: New York institutions already fund employee transportation at scale — intercampus shuttles, guaranteed-ride programs, tenant buses. One of the city's largest hospital systems already runs an employee water shuttle. The behavior is proven. What's been missing is a vessel built for it.
copy.stripe_lesson: We ran the first employer water commute on San Francisco Bay. The ride worked; the vessel was the lesson — an 8-seat executive boat is not a commuter line. The 20-seat N45 is built for exactly this: a scheduled line your team can set a watch by, with a seat that works like a desk.
copy.loi_cta: Two ways to bring a line to your people. Option A — sponsor a line: your institution underwrites a scheduled service, your name on the hull optional (indicative from ~$125K per month). Option B — commit seats: reserve seats at $750–900 per seat-month and we aggregate your line's launch. Both start with a non-binding letter of intent: it costs nothing, commits nothing, and tells us which line to build first.
copy.price_anchor: less than the parking space it replaces
copy.launch_trigger: A line launches when about 60–72 seats are committed — enough for a real commuter service.
copy.problem_title: The congestion charge is the tax. The water is the spare lane.
copy.problem_lead: Your people already live and work on the water. Roads and tolls take the rest. Electric hydrofoils cut that tax — terminal to terminal, above the traffic.
copy.proof_title: New York already funds the water commute.
copy.proof_lead: Institutions run employee shuttles — including on the water. We bring the vessel class that makes a network pencil.
copy.proof_worked_body: New York institutions already fund employee transportation at scale — intercampus shuttles, guaranteed-ride programs, tenant buses. One of the city's largest hospital systems already runs an employee water shuttle. The behavior is proven. What's been missing is a vessel built for it.
copy.proof_fixed_body: We ran the first employer water commute on San Francisco Bay. The ride worked; the vessel was the lesson — an 8-seat executive boat is not a commuter line. The 20-seat N45 is built for exactly this: a scheduled line your team can set a watch by, with a seat that works like a desk.
copy.proof_ask_body: A non-binding letter of intent — sponsor a line or commit seats — so we sequence the network on real demand.
copy.network_lead: Trunk lines, feeders, and express corridors on real landings. Use the phase control for launch vs full build-out. Seasonal East End is a separate layer.
